challenges.name: Clean Load-Out
challenges.note: No corrections anywhere on the dock

challenges.name: Steady Travel
challenges.note: Travel speed held the whole run

hazards.no-chock-entry: You drove into a trailer that was not chocked or dock-locked. A trailer creeps a few inches every time a truck enters; a driver hooks up and pulls away with you inside; the plate drops and the truck goes four feet to the yard.
hazards.ramp-forward-loaded: You drove forward down the ramp with a load. On a grade the load points downhill and the truck tips over the front axle; loaded, you go up forward and down in reverse.
hazards.ride-forks: You let a coworker ride on the forks. A forklift has one seat and one belt; a person on the forks has neither, and the mast, the load and the overhead guard are all built on the assumption nobody is there.
hazards.under-raised-load: You walked under the raised load. Forks fail, chains stretch, pallets break — nothing that is lifted is ever stood under, and nothing raised is left unattended.

interrupts.alert: The trailer has walked forward off the plate. There is daylight opening at the dock lip behind you and you are standing in the box.
interrupts.cue: Get the trailer locked to the building again.
interrupts.missNote: The gap kept opening while you worked. Trailer separation puts the plate into the gap and the truck four feet down onto the yard, upside down, with the operator underneath it — it is the single most common way a dock kills somebody.
interrupts.why: Trailers creep a few inches with every pass of a truck, and the gap only has to reach the length of the plate. The restraint is what holds the trailer to the building; chocks alone slide on a wet apron.
interrupts.wrongNote: It is the dock lock. A trailer moving away from the building while you are inside it is the only thing happening on this dock.

interrupts.alert: A picker has stepped out of the racking into your aisle, on your blind side behind the load.
interrupts.cue: Warn them before you are any closer.
interrupts.missNote: You kept travelling with somebody in the aisle behind the load. Pedestrians struck by forklifts are almost never seen first by the operator — that is the point of the horn at every blind corner, not just the ones with a mirror.
interrupts.why: A loaded mast blocks the line of sight in exactly the direction of travel, so the operator is the last person to see a pedestrian and the pedestrian assumes they have been seen. The horn is the only part of the truck that works around a load.
interrupts.wrongNote: It is the horn. Somebody is in your path on the side you cannot see, and every second of travel closes the distance.

lateNotes.dock-plate: The plate goes down only onto a trailer that is chocked and locked; a plate on a loose trailer is the gap you drive into.
lateNotes.rack-height: Rack height is set at the rack, stopped, with the mast vertical — not while travelling.
lateNotes.throttle: Travel comes after the load is under, tilted back and low — a raised load on the move is the tip-over.

name: Forklift Dock

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Check today's truck, the load-out order and the capacity plate.
steps.prompt: Check today's truck, the load-out order and the capacity plate.
steps.title: Read the pre-shift checklist
steps.why: The checklist is the record that the truck was inspected before the shift; the capacity plate is the number every load is measured against.

steps.cue: Walk the truck: tires, fork heels and tips, mast chains and hoses, horn and lights.
steps.prompt: Walk the truck: tires, fork heels and tips, mast chains and hoses, horn and lights.
steps.title: Pre-shift inspection
steps.why: A forklift with a cracked fork heel or a slack chain fails under the load it lifts, not in the yard. A truck that fails inspection is tagged out, not driven gently.

steps.cue: Sit, and fasten the seatbelt before the key turns.
steps.prompt: Sit, and fasten the seatbelt before the key turns.
steps.title: Belt on
steps.why: In a tip-over the overhead guard protects a belted operator. An unbelted one jumps, and the guard lands on them — the single biggest killer of forklift operators.

steps.cue: Chock the trailer wheels and engage the dock lock on the rear impact guard — both, before the plate.
steps.prompt: Chock the trailer wheels and engage the dock lock on the rear impact guard — both, before the plate.
steps.title: Secure the trailer
steps.why: The chock stops creep; the lock stops a driver pulling away. Either one alone is the accident the other would have prevented.

steps.cue: Bring the dock plate down and seat its lip on the trailer bed.

drag.missNote: The lip is not on the bed — seat it square on the trailer floor.

steps.prompt: Bring the dock plate down and seat its lip on the trailer bed.
steps.title: Set the dock plate
steps.why: The plate bridges the gap and the height difference. It sits on the trailer bed by at least four inches of lip, on a trailer that cannot move.

steps.cue: Look down the trailer: floor sound, nose supported, lights on.
steps.prompt: Look down the trailer: floor sound, nose supported, lights on.
steps.title: Check the trailer floor and nose
steps.why: A trailer floor rots from the inside. The truck weighs three times the load; a soft floor lets it through, and a dropped trailer with no landing-gear support noses down with the truck inside.

steps.cue: Read the pallet weight and load centre against the capacity plate — commit when it is inside the rating.

gauge.label: LOAD vs RATING
gauge.missNote: Outside the rating at this load centre — split the load or get a bigger truck.

steps.prompt: Read the pallet weight and load centre against the capacity plate — commit when it is inside the rating.
steps.title: Check the load against the plate
steps.why: The plate rates the truck at a 24-inch load centre. A long pallet moves the centre out and the rating down; the pallet that is 'about right' is the one that tips.

steps.cue: Forks fully under to the heel, mast tilted back, then raise only to travel height — four to six inches.
steps.outOfOrderNote: Under, then back, then up — the load is settled before it leaves the floor.
steps.prompt: Forks fully under to the heel, mast tilted back, then raise only to travel height — four to six inches.
steps.title: Pick the load
steps.why: Under to the heel so the load cannot slide; back so it rests against the carriage; low so the centre of gravity stays inside the wheelbase.

steps.cue: Hold a steady walking-pace speed, horn at the door, load low and back.
steps.holdBreakNote: Speed out of band — settle it to walking pace and hold.
steps.prompt: Hold a steady walking-pace speed, horn at the door, load low and back.
steps.title: Travel to the trailer
steps.why: A forklift stops in its own length only at walking pace. The horn at every door and aisle end is the pedestrian's only warning.

steps.cue: Loaded, descend the yard ramp in reverse — load uphill, looking over your shoulder.
steps.prompt: Loaded, descend the yard ramp in reverse — load uphill, looking over your shoulder.
steps.title: Take the ramp in reverse
steps.why: Loaded, the load faces uphill: forward up, reverse down. That keeps the weight over the drive axle and the load against the carriage instead of sliding off the tips.

steps.cue: Stopped at the rack, mast vertical, raise until the forks clear the beam — commit inside the band.

gauge.label: FORKS vs BEAM
gauge.missNote: Under the beam or too far over — adjust before you move in.

steps.prompt: Stopped at the rack, mast vertical, raise until the forks clear the beam — commit inside the band.
steps.title: Set the forks to the rack beam
steps.why: Two inches over the beam clears it; a foot over is a load that drops onto the beam and a pallet that breaks. The height is set stopped, never while the truck is moving.

steps.cue: Look at the plate, the chock and the lock, and click what has moved.

itemNotes.trailer-creep: The trailer has crept away from the dock: there is daylight between the plate lip and the bed — stop, re-chock, re-seat the plate.

steps.prompt: Look at the plate, the chock and the lock, and click what has moved.
steps.title: Walk the dock before the next load
steps.why: Every entry pushes the trailer. The dock is checked between loads, not at the end of the shift.

tagline: Dock load-out: pre-shift inspection, belt on, trailer chocked and dock-locked before the plate, load against the capacity plate, forks under and mast back, low and steady, ramp in reverse, rack height, and the trailer that crept
